feed.title: General Motors (GM) Has One Operational US EV Battery Plant
feed.summary: General Motors (GM) now has only one operational US electric vehicle battery plant, reflecting a shift in its North American manufacturing strategy. The company is scaling back EV battery production in the US while investing C$144 million to expand pickup truck assembly in Canada, focusing on higher-margin models. This move suggests GM is prioritizing profitable trucks and near-term cash generation, potentially slowing its EV progress in North America, a key point for investors to consider.

feed.title: Why did developers change their proposal for the Inola aluminum smelter?
feed.summary: Developers of the proposed Inola aluminum smelter have reduced their fluoride emission limit by 37% following concerns from the Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality and local communities. Century Aluminum executive Matt Aboud explained that this change, along with further environmental testing, aims to address community safety concerns and meet "world-class" standards for the $4 billion project. The developers are also highlighting the project's potential to create thousands of jobs and bolster the U.S. aluminum industry.

feed.title: FHFA Criticizes FICO; Credit Bureaus Stocks Slide
feed.summary: Federal Housing Finance Agency Director Bill Pulte's posts on X, criticizing credit score pricing and the practices of Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion, led to significant stock declines for Fair Isaac (FICO), Equifax, and TransUnion. Pulte suggested the use of "bi-merge" reports, pushed for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to approve VantageScore for all lenders, and indicated studies into using a single credit report to reduce consumer costs. Analysts have varied opinions on the long-term impact, but the comments highlight potential shifts in the credit scoring industry that could affect revenue models for these companies.
